sources.cite: NASEMSO. National Model EMS Clinical Guidelines, Version 3.0 (March 2022): Respiratory Distress (Includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema); Airway Management
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the full text Iowa HHS hosts (https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/198/download) through summarizing fetches with quotes; NASEMSO's own page, read the same day, still presents Version 3 (2022) as current and names no later version. Albuterol nebulized for bronchospasm, repeated for ongoing distress; noninvasive ventilation (CPAP) for severe distress, considered early; start PEEP at 5 cmH2O and raise in 2-3 cmH2O steps to the lowest effective pressure; if the patient worsens on CPAP (worse mental status, rising EtCO2, vomiting), 'remove CPAP/BiPAP and escalate airway management options'; target SpO2 94-98%, and 'permissive hypoxia (SPO2 >= 90%) may be appropriate in patients with COPD'; avoid nitrates within 48 hours of a phosphodiesterase inhibitor. The guideline's albuterol dose for distress (5 mg) is above the inhalation solution's labeled 2.5 mg; the case uses the labeled 2.5 mg dose, repeated.

sources.cite: NHTSA. National EMS Scope of Practice Model 2019: Including Change Notices 1.0 and 2.0 (DOT HS 813 151, 2021-08-01)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17: the record page (title, report number, date; the change notices add intramuscular injection, vaccination in a public health emergency and nasal swab collection at EMT and above) and the PDF's skill tables through a summarizing fetch whose table columns were partly unclear, so placement was checked against the course's own reading (backend/supabase/seed/labs/ems-sources.ts, 2026-11-09) and REQ-241's reading (2026-11-11). EMR: oxygen, BVM, naloxone (intranasal or auto-injector), unit-dose hazmat antidote auto-injectors, tourniquet, wound packing, emergency moves, manual stabilization; no pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring or transport. EMT adds pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring, oral glucose, aspirin, the patient's own nitroglycerin, an inhaled bronchodilator, CPAP, the epinephrine auto-injector. AEMT adds IV and IO access, non-medicated IV fluids, supraglottic airways, waveform capnography, sublingual nitroglycerin and a limited list of IV and IM drugs (dextrose, naloxone). Paramedic adds 12-lead interpretation, manual defibrillation, synchronized cardioversion, transcutaneous pacing, needle chest decompression, intubation and medicated infusions. No newer model was found on 2026-11-17.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

His blood pressure (102/66 at first) and its fall after a sublingual nitroglycerin dose taken within a day of sildenafil (about 30 mmHg) and its rise with each 250 mL bolus (about 12 mmHg) are authored FLAG figures in the direction the sources give. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

brief.situation: 06:40. You are an AEMT on an ambulance with an EMT partner. Frank, 64, woke with chest pressure 30 minutes ago. He is pale and sweaty.
handover: You carry aspirin 81 mg chewable tablets, nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual tablets, IV supplies and normal saline, oxygen, and a monitor that acquires and transmits a 12-lead (the receiving physician interprets it).
A PCI center is 20 minutes away; a community hospital without a cath lab is 7 minutes away.
Within AEMT scope: aspirin, sublingual nitroglycerin, IV access and fluids, 12-lead acquisition and transmission. No 12-lead interpretation and no other cardiac drugs.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated seconds per real second. Pause any time.
Every assessment and treatment takes the time it would on a real call. Scene time and the drive run on the clock.
Partway through you are asked to explain your decisions in writing. The case ends when care is handed over, then a debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Why did (or should) Frank not get nitroglycerin, and what did you give instead?

parts.label: The contraindications
parts.criteria: Sildenafil within 24 hours (tadalafil 48), a marginal systolic pressure around 100 and an inferior STEMI with likely right ventricular involvement: nitroglycerin can drop his pressure dangerously, so it is withheld.
parts.modelAnswer: He took sildenafil last night, his pressure is only about 100, and the physician read an inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement. Any one makes nitroglycerin risky; together it is out.

parts.label: Instead
parts.criteria: Aspirin chewed, 12-lead acquired and transmitted within 10 minutes, IV access, fluid boluses with lung checks for low pressure, the PCI center with the cath lab activated.
parts.modelAnswer: Aspirin, the 12-lead transmitted early, an IV with small boluses for his pressure while checking his lungs, and the PCI center with the cath lab ready.

expertPath.text: Monitor and vital signs (102/66), aspirin 324 mg chewed, 12-lead acquired and transmitted; history with the direct question: sildenafil last night.
No nitroglycerin: sildenafil within 24 hours and a marginal pressure. IV access.
Physician: inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement; to the PCI center. Small boluses for low pressure, checking his lungs.

pci.headline: The right drug was no drug
pci.body: Sildenafil last night, a pressure around 100 and an inferior STEMI: nitroglycerin was out. Aspirin, the 12-lead early, an IV and the cath lab were in.

arrived.headline: Arrived, by a harder route
arrived.body: Check the nitrate, the destination and how fast the 12-lead went out.

crashed.headline: A nitrate on top of sildenafil
crashed.body: Ask every chest pain patient about erectile dysfunction pills before nitroglycerin, and treat a marginal pressure as a stop sign. If the pressure falls: flat, legs up, fluid boluses.

scoring.modelReasoning: Chest pressure with sweating at 64 is ACS until shown otherwise: aspirin 324 mg chewed, a 12-lead acquired and transmitted within 10 minutes, IV access. Before any nitroglycerin, ask about phosphodiesterase inhibitors: sildenafil within 24 hours (tadalafil 48) contraindicates nitrates, and so does a low or marginal pressure; an inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement adds risk. Withhold it; treat low pressure with small fluid boluses and lung checks; take him to the PCI center with the cath lab activated by the physician who read the transmission.

pde.ask: While you take the history: which answer rules out nitroglycerin for Frank?
pde.explain: NASEMSO: no nitrate after a phosphodiesterase inhibitor (sildenafil within 24 hours, tadalafil 48), or with hypotension.
